meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.claim: Growth hormone / IGF-1 axis activates PI3K
data.mechanism: IGF-1 docks on the IGF-1 receptor, which recruits IRS proteins and switches on PI3K to make the lipid messenger PIP3. Growth hormone does not use this receptor: it signals through its own receptor and JAK2/STAT5b, and reaches this arm mostly by inducing hepatic IGF-1. The node is drawn as one axis because the Atlas's lifespan evidence comes from interventions that lower the whole axis at once.
data.mechanism_beginner: IGF-1 latches onto its own receptor and switches on PI3K, which builds a signalling lipid. Growth hormone works one step further back: it does not land on this receptor itself, it makes the liver release IGF-1, which then does. Insulin takes a receptor of its own into the same arm.
data.boundary: Compressed on purpose: growth hormone and IGF-1 are one node here, but they are not one molecule and they do not share a receptor. GH signals GHR-JAK2-STAT5b and acts on this arm largely by inducing hepatic IGF-1; patients with a homozygous STAT5b mutation have GH insensitivity with low IGF-1 and low IGFBP-3 (Kofoed 2003, PMID 13679528, outside this corpus). The dwarf-mouse lifespan evidence on this axis lowers GH and IGF-1 together, so it does not tell the two apart. Insulin enters the same arm through its own receptor and is drawn separately (INS-PI3K).
